findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — get_item_key() applies math.floor/math.ceil to the audit log’s datetime field, raising TypeError when constructing cursors for nonempty optimized results. Preserve DateTimePaginator’s datetime-to-cursor conversion.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:883 — Advanced pagination passes negative offsets directly into a QuerySet slice, which Django rejects, causing an exception instead of returning a page. Validate offsets or implement reverse traversal using supported query operations.

goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same underlying problem as the golden comment - that negative slice offsets are being passed to Django QuerySets, which Django does not support and will cause an error. While the golden comment specifically mentions OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py and the candidate points to src/sentry/api/paginator.py:883, they are describing the same fundamental bug: negative slicing on Django querysets causing exceptions. The candidate correctly identifies that Django rejects negative offsets and suggests validation or alternative implementation.
